text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on October 28 in history.
1017 - Henry III, German King and Holy Roman Emperor, born. He ascended to the German throne in 1039 and became Holy Roman Emperor in 1043.
1492 - Christopher Columbus discovered Cuba and claimed it in the name of Spain.
1627 - Jahangir, Mughal emperor of India, died on his way to Lahore. Emperor from 1605, he became famed for his patronage of the arts.
1628 - After being besieged for months, Huguenots at La Rochelle capitulated to troops of the French crown under Cardinal Richelieu.
1636 - Harvard College founded at Cambridge, Massachusetts.
1746 - The Peruvian cities of Lima and Callao were demolished by an earthquake, killing at least 18,000.
1846 - Georges Auguste Escoffier born. A French chef known as "The King of Chefs and Chef of Kings", he achieved his worldwide reputation when he worked at London's Savoy and Carlton hotels.
1886 - The Statue of Liberty, a gift from France designed by Auguste Bartholdi, was dedicated by President Grover Cleveland.
1891 - An earthquake struck the Niphon Islands in Japan, killing 10,000 people and leaving at least 300,000 homeless.
1914 - U.S. microbiologist Jonas Edward Salk, who developed the first polio vaccine in 1953, born.

1918 - The Czechoslovak state came into being when the Prague national committee took over land upon the dissolution of Austria-Hungary. The Republic was declared in November 1918 under President Masaryk.
1932 - Spyros Kyprianou born. When Cyprus gained independence, he was its first foreign minister and took over as president after the death of Archbishop Makarios.
1940 - Italian forces under Mussolini crossed into Greece from occupied Albania in an attempt to occupy the country.
1952 - William Hughes, Australian prime minister from 1915-23, died,
1958 - Cardinal Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli, Patriarch of Venice, was elected Pope and took the title John XXIII.
1962 - The Cuban missile crisis ended when Soviet leader Khrushchev said its missiles would be dismantled and returned to the USSR. The U.S. then said it would lift its blockade of Cuba.
1971 - By a vote of 356-244, the British House of Commons voted in favour of joining the European Economic Community.
1981 - A Soviet Whiskey-class submarine armed with nuclear weapons ran aground in Swedish waters. The vessel was released on November 6 after protests to the USSR.
1982 - The Spanish Socialist Workers' Party led by Felipe Gonzalez won a landslide victory in a general election.
1988 - Pietro Annigoni, portrait painter (notably of Queen Elizabeth) died.
